The claimant claimed that he was employed with Limra Water Supply and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the fracture of left tibia and wasting of left quadriceps muscles, he was out of employment and was disabled.
Hence, he filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation from the Corporation.
4. The Corporation denied the accident as well as negligence on the part of the driver of the bus belonging to it.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as P.W.1 and he marked Exs.P.1 to P.14.
He also examined a doctor as P.W.2, who deposed that the claimant suffered fracture of tibia and that he was admitted as an inpatient for ten days.
He deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 40% to the limb and whole body.

The Corporation examined its driver as R.W.1, who deposed that it was the claimant,
who was responsible for the accident.
6. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the driver of the bus belonging to the Corporation was negligent and was responsible for the accident.
It held that the claimant had suffered fracture of tibia and wastage of the left quadriceps muscles, which affected his day- to-day activities.

Considering the evidence of P.W.2 that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 40% to the whole body, the Tribunal assessed the disability at 13.33% to the whole body and his income was considered at a sum of Rs.13,250/- per month and his age at 18 years and the following compensation was awarded:

sentences.text:
The Tribunal directed the Corporation to pay compensation along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of clam petition till its realization.
Being aggrieved by the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant is in appeal.
The Corporation is also in appeal challenging the liability on the ground that the claimant was negligent.
8. Learned counsel for the claimant contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads warrants enhancement as the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meager.

Per contra, learned counsel for the Corporation contended that the claimant was negligent and was responsible for the accident and R.W.1 clearly spoke about the manner of the accident and the Tribunal did not consider the same.
She also contended that the claimant did not possess a valid licence and therefore probablising that he had no skill in riding and had thus the claimant contributed to the accident.
10. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant as well as the learned counsel for the Corporation.

11. Having regard to the finding of the Tribunal that the claimant had suffered fracture of tibia and wasting of muscles, the assessment of disability at 13.33% to the whole body appears to be just and reasonable, likewise, the Tribunal had considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.13,250/- per month which is also reasonable.
Consequently, the compensation awarded towards loss of income due to disability and medical expenses are just and proper.
However, the compensation awarded under other heads being meager, NC: 2023:KHC-K:5560 deserves to be marginally enhanced.
Hence, the compensation to which the claimant is entitled to is re

In so far as the liability to pay compensation is concerned, the claimant contended that he was a pillion rider on a motorcycle and that the driver of the bus belonging to the Corporation without Dawood Nadaf S/O Syed Nadaf vs The Managing Director on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156830110/

sentences.text: The corporation did not lead any evidence to demonstrate that the claimant was negligent.
The evidence of R.W.1 being interested testimony, the same did not help the Corporation to establish that the claimant was negligent.
In that view of the matter, the Corporation is liable to pay compensation along with interest.
In view of the above, MFA No.201642/2021 filed by the claimant is allowed in part and MFA No.200667/2022 filed by the Corporation is dismissed.
14. The compensation of Rs.5,21,950/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.5,75,200/-.
15. The Corporation is directed to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
16. The Corporation shall deposit the compensation along with interest before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
17. Amount in deposit in MFA No.200667/2022 is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
